references.text: Jealousy is described as a man's rage, reflecting the intense emotional reaction linked to suspicion of infidelity.
Jealousy is mentioned as a destructive force, stronger than anger, highlighting the seriousness of the 'spirit of jealousy'.
Jealousy is described as hard as Sheol, illustrating the intense nature of this emotion in a marital context.
Summary of the law concerning jealousy, referring back to the situation described in verse 14.
Prohibition against sexual immorality with another man's wife, which forms the basis for the suspicion of impurity mentioned in the verse.
The penalty for adultery under the law, demonstrating the seriousness of the potential impurity being investigated.
Parallel law regarding adultery, relevant to understanding what it means for a woman to have become unclean.
